title: McCord's letter to Judge Sirica

tellings.quote: mcord M mcord out of our office is the one that gets pissed off over the fact that he thinks they're all getting sold down the stream here

plain: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer, tells of a 1973 letter that James McCord, one of the men arrested in the Watergate break-in (the scandal that brought down President Nixon), wrote to John Sirica, the judge hearing the case in Washington DC. Sheehan says McCord, connected to his own office, got angry because he believed the defendants were all being sold down the river, and that this is what led him to write. If true, it would place Sheehan's circle close to a turning point of the scandal.
